records.title: How are Nevada ballots counted and verified?
records.retrieval_query: What election, jurisdiction, and ballot-counting process does the statement refer to?

passages.P1: # How are Nevada ballots counted and verified?
passages.P2: Nearly 600,000 of Nevada’s general election votes have been cast by mail in this election — about half of all reported votes. That’s more mail ballots than have ever been cast in any previous election in the state.
passages.P3: Elections experts have said mail-in ballots are safe, and Nevada’s Republican Secretary of State Barbara Cegavske testified this year that her office did not find any fraud during the state’s primary election, which was conducted almost entirely by mail.
passages.P4: Under Assembly Bill 4, passed during a special session of the Legislature in August, all active registered voters in Nevada were sent a mail ballot.
passages.P5: Here are details of the ballot counting and verification process, according to information provided by the Nevada secretary of state’s office.
passages.P7: Ballots in Nevada are counted by local elections officials, the county clerk or the county registrar of voters and their staffs. Statewide, voter registrations are overseen by Secretary of State Barbara Cegavske, who works with local officials to ensure elections are conducted properly. Under state law, observers are allowed to watch the counting process, and have done so in this election.
passages.P9: All mail ballots in Clark County were counted first by running them through a digital scanner. If the scanner cannot read the ballot or determine the voter’s intent, the ballot is sent to an adjudication or duplication team, both of which are overseen by a bipartisan election board. County elections officials have said about 70 percent of ballots are sent to be reviewed by elections officials.
passages.P10: Related: Biden has widened lead over Trump in Nevada
passages.P11: All voting equipment used in the state, including mail ballot scanners, has to meet or exceed the federal voting system standards. It also must be independently tested to determine it functions correctly. Independent testing is performed by the Nevada Gaming Control Board.
passages.P12: Clark County uses the Agilis ballot counting technology.
passages.P14: All mail ballots had to be postmarked by Nov. 3 or dropped off at a ballot drop-off location by 7 p.m. on Election Day in order to be counted. Counties have until seven days (Nov. 10) after the election to receive ballots in the mail, but only ballots postmarked on or before Election Day will be counted.
passages.P15: Ballots received by the county in the mail without a postmark, or with an illegible postmark, will be considered mailed by Election Day, but only if they were received by Nov. 6. The deadline for counting all ballots is Nov. 12. After that, the final canvass of the vote will happen on Nov. 16 when state officials review the results.
passages.P17: Ballot envelopes are individually bar coded to specific voters and printed on special paper that makes them impossible to counterfeit easily. Officials verify signatures on the outside of ballot envelopes and set aside those that don’t match for further investigation. An electronic system also prevents people from casting more than one vote.
passages.P18: All mail ballots had to be returned in an authorized ballot return envelope, which had to be signed by the voter. That signature is compared to the signature on file at the election office. If the signature does not match, the ballot is rejected.

passages.P2: # Appeals court rejects DOJ request for California to set aside disputed ballots allegedly sent to 'noncitzen' voters
passages.P5: The 9th Circuit Court of Appeals on Friday rejected the Justice Department's request for California to set aside disputed ballots sent to alleged noncitizen voters.
passages.P7: LOS ANGELES -- The 9th Circuit Court of Appeals on Friday rejected the Justice Department's request for California to set aside disputed ballots received in the midterm election.
passages.P8: The panel's 2-1 ruling is the latest setback for the Trump administration's efforts to assert control over state-run elections.
passages.P9: The administration has alleged California sent ballots to some 20,000 people who may not be U.S. citizens. It wants the state to set those ballots aside and not count them until citizenship can be verified. California officials say the list is highly unreliable and likely includes many people who are U.S. citizens.
passages.P10: A district court judge already forcefully denied that request and warned that the Justice Department's demands could disenfranchise citizens.
passages.P11: "As the district court found - and we discern no clear error - there is no feasible way to identify and segregate the ballots of specific individuals without potentially catastrophic effects on the entire system," the appeals court wrote.
passages.P12: The ruling is the latest in an expansive legal battle between the federal government and the state before Election Day in the midterms Tuesday. Millions of people in California have already voted.
passages.P13: The majority opinion was authored by Judge Mark J. Bennett, who was appointed by President Donald Trump, and Judge Gabriel P. Sanchez, who was appointed by former President Joe Biden.
passages.P14: The Justice Department did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the ruling.
passages.P15: Hundreds of thousands of ballots have already been processed. Elections officials have said that processed votes are completely anonymized and can't be matched back to the voters who submitted them.
passages.P16: The ruling comes during broader federal scrutiny of local elections, with the Trump administration issuing a raft of subpoenas in Alaska in a spoiler-candidate controversy. The Justice Department has also provided a list of alleged noncitizen voters to officials in Washington state.
passages.P17: ## Outside groups sued for access to the disputed list
passages.P18: Earlier on Friday, a federal judge in Washington ordered the Trump administration to share the disputed list of names with lawyers for the Coalition for Humane Immigrant Rights and the UCLA Voting Rights Project. They want the list so they can examine who is on the list and assess its impact on eligible voters.
passages.P19: It will be the first time that a nongovernment organization will have the opportunity to evaluate the merits of the list of some 20,000 names.
passages.P20: Prosecutors with the Trump administration have argued that there is just as much to lose from noncitizens illegally voting, arguing that to tally those votes would dilute the voice of citizens.
passages.P21: Democratic gubernatorial candidate Xavier Becerra is an adviser to the UCLA Voting Rights Project.

passages.P3: # DOJ Subpoenas California Election Officials, Despite Judge’s Order to Stop Threatening Them
passages.P4: A federal judge warned federal prosecutors to stop threatening California election officials, but prosecutors kept going.
passages.P7: Jeanne Kuang, Ryan Sabalow, Sergio Olmos, CalMatters
passages.P8: A poll worker prepares mail-in ballots for sorting at the Contra Costa County Elections Operation Center in Martinez on March 5, 2024. (Martin do Nascimento/KQED)
passages.P9: *This story was originally published by CalMatters. Sign up for their newsletters.*
passages.P10: On Wednesday, a federal judge issued a blistering order warning federal prosecutors to stop threatening California election officials with crimes.
passages.P11: A day later, federal prosecutors kept going.
passages.P12: At least four elections workers in California have received federal criminal grand jury subpoenas over the past week, with at least one delivered on Thursday after the court’s order.
passages.P13: In that subpoena, issued to the Orange County Registrar of Voters’s office, federal agents with the Department of Homeland Security are seeking unredacted voter records for 60 people, according to records obtained by CalMatters.
passages.P14: Colby Brown, rover supervisor at the Veterans Memorial Center voting center, seals a ballot drop box, in Davis on June 2, 2026. (Gina Castro/KQED)
passages.P15: The subpoenas signal an intensification of the federal government’s unprecedented targeting of California’s elections, setting up what could be a showdown over the fundamentals of American democracy around next Tuesday’s midterm elections.
passages.P16: The prosecutors include those in the office of Los Angeles’ top federal prosecutor, Bill Essayli, a leading aide in President Donald Trump’s push to find evidence to support longstanding — and never proven — claims that California elections are rigged in Democrats’ favor due to noncitizen votes.
passages.P17: Bloomberg Law first reported Thursday that U.S. Justice Department leaders had directed top federal prosecutors to pursue criminal subpoenas of state and local officials in their efforts to find evidence that noncitizens were allowed to vote. The news outlet cited two unnamed sources familiar with the situation.
passages.P18: This month Essayli sued California and Los Angeles County, demanding they set aside the ballots of 20,000 registered voters he accused of not being U.S. citizens, and last week the Justice Department sent letters threatening local elections officials with criminal charges if they did not do the same with lists of voters in their own counties.
passages.P19: County election officials from across California have said spot checks found the government’s list of names to be inaccurate and have challenged the legality of the requests. Officials in only one county so far – San Luis Obispo – have announced they will investigate the voters from the Justice Department’s demand letters.
passages.P21: In Los Angeles County, federal prosecutors last week subpoenaed three employees of the Registrar-Recorder’s Office, ordering them to testify before a grand jury in a criminal investigation on Nov. 4, the day after the election.
passages.P22: Prosecutors demanded county employees bring records of how their department prevents non-citizens from voting and “records relating to or involving evidence collected by your agency which tends to indicate an alien has voted in a federal election.”

passages.P1: # Read: Full transcript of Donald Trump’s call to Brad Raffensperger
passages.P2: ##### The infamous conversation has become a focal point of Fulton DA Fani Willis’ investigation into alleged election interference in Georgia
passages.P3: ATLANTA, Ga. (Atlanta News First) - On Jan. 2, 2021, then-President Donald Trump and his White House placed a call to Georgia Secretary of State Brad Raffensperger over the outcome of the state’s 2020 presidential election results.
passages.P4: That call has become a crucial part of Fulton County DA Fani Willis’ investigation into whether Trump or any of his associates interfered with the election’s outcome, an election that saw Joe Biden become the first Democrat to win Georgia since Bill Clinton in 1992.
passages.P5: Here is a transcript of that phone call, provided by the Associated Press:
passages.P6: Call Operator: I’m just here to conference you in with Secretary Raffensperger and Mr. Germany. We’re going to conference you through to POTUS shortly.
passages.P7: Jordan Fuchs: Great. Thank you so much.
passages.P8: Call Operator: OK, Jordan, do you mind? How do you pronounce your last name, Jordan? I’m sorry.
passages.P9: Jordan Fuchs: Yeah, I get that a lot. It’s OK. It’s Fuchs.
passages.P10: Call Operator: Fuchs. Ok. Ok. Thank you. I’ll go ahead and announce you to Secretary Raffensperger and Mr. Germany. Thank you so much ma’am. Ms. Fuchs you are now connected to the other gentlemen.
passages.P12: Brad Raffensperger: Hi, Jordan. This is Brad.
passages.P17: Fuchs: Mark Meadows told me that their lawyers are going to be on the call too.
passages.P19: Call Operator: Everyone, I’m going to conference you through to POTUS momentarily. One moment.
passages.P21: Call Operator: The conference is now connected.
passages.P23: Mark Meadows: Mr. Raffensperger, are you on the line?
passages.P24: Ryan Germany: He was here a second ago. This is Ryan Germany.
passages.P25: Mark Meadows: Mr. Germany, Ms. Fuchs
passages.P26: Brad Raffensperger: And Brad Raffensperger here.
passages.P27: Mark Meadows: OK, all right. So, Mr. President, everybody is on the line. And just so this is Mark Meadows, the chief of staff. Just so we all are aware, on the line is secretary of state and two other individuals, Jordan and Mr. Germany. With him, you also have the attorneys that represent the president, Kurt and Alex and Cleta Mitchell, who is not the attorney of record, but has been Trump involved. Myself and then the president. Mr. President, now I’ll turn it over to you.
passages.P28: President Donald Trump: OK, thank you very much. Hello, Brad and Ryan and everybody. We appreciate the time and the call. So we’ve spent a lot of time on this. And if we could just go over some of the numbers, I think it’s pretty clear that we won. We won very substantially, Georgia. You even see it by rally side, frankly, we’d be getting 25-- 30,000 people a rally and the competition would get less than 100 people. And it never made sense.

passages.P1: # Trump’s speech claiming US election vulnerabilities, annotated
passages.P3: President Donald Trump tried to convince Americans in a primetime address Thursday night that their elections are vulnerable to fraud and need immediate attention. While he did not repeat his frequent mantra that he actually won the presidential election he lost in 2020, Trump did declassify documents he said showed an influence campaign by China, a coverup by US intelligence officials and fraud in Michigan.
passages.P4: The evidence, offered mostly in highly redacted out-of-context emails, did not live up to those claims. But it will certainly be grist for Trump’s efforts to curtail mail-in voting and add new voter ID requirements.
passages.P5: The speech, along with context, is below.
passages.P6: Good evening. Before we begin, I'm proud to report that our country is safer, stronger, and far wealthier than it has ever been before. We are doing great. Less than two years ago, we inherited an economic and social disaster after the worst inflation in 48 years, the wide open borders with millions and millions of people pouring in from all over the world, including criminals of all types, and 11,888 murderers, many of whom killed more than one person.
passages.P7: We had transgender for everybody, men in women's sports, crime ravaging our cities, and the whole world was laughing at us as a nation, but not anymore. Two years ago, our country was dead. Now, we are the hottest country anywhere in the world. America is respected like we have never been respected before.
passages.P8: This speech was billed as a major address on election security. It’s starting with some standard Trump talking points.
passages.P9: We have more money being invested in the United States than at any time in the history of our country. More Americans are working today than ever before. This week, it was announced that inflation saw the largest monthly decline in more than six years, just happened. It was just given out. The media reported it and we accept it, the best in six years.
passages.P10: The tax cuts in our Great Big Beautiful Bill are saving hardworking families thousands and thousands of dollars, like with the provisions, no tax on tips, no tax on overtime and no tax on Social Security for our great seniors, along with the interest deduction on a loan used to purchase a car, but only if that car is made in America.
passages.P11: And a 100 percent expensing for our job-creating businesses. Our stock markets are at their highest point in many years, but we can actually say of all time. And your 401(k)s, pensions and retirement accounts are setting records every single day, the highest in history. For years we paid the highest price for prescription drugs anywhere in the world.
passages.P12: Now we pay the lowest price under my Most-Favored-Nations policy, because I was able to get the rest of the world and the pharmaceutical companies to act responsibly. Drug prices are coming down by 70, 80 and 90 percent. Trumprx.gov, this will ultimately reduce the cost of health care. You have to go to Trumprx.gov and take advantage of it. But the cost of health care is coming way down because of what we've done with prescription drugs.
